                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  defmodule ChangingNothingExcept do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    use Ash.Policy.SimpleCheck\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    def match?(_actor, %{subject: %Ash.Changeset{} = changeset}, opts) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      allowed = opts[:attributes]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      {:ok, Enum.all?(Map.keys(changeset.attributes), &(&1 in allowed))}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    def match?(_, _, _), do: {:ok, true}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  @moduledoc """\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  A behaviour for declaring checks, which can be used to easily construct\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  authorization rules.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  If a check can be expressed simply, i.e as a function of the actor, or the context of the request,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  see `Ash.Policy.SimpleCheck` for an easy way to write that check.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  If a check can be expressed with a filter statement, see `Ash.Policy.FilterCheck`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  for an easy way to write that check.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  """\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @type actor :: any\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @type options :: Keyword.t()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @type authorizer :: Ash.Policy.Authorizer.t()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @type check_type :: :simple | :filter | :manual\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @type ref :: {module(), Keyword.t()} | module()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  defstruct [:check, :check_module, :check_opts, :type, :__spark_metadata__]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @doc false\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  def transform(%{check: {check_module, opts}} = policy) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    case init(check_module, opts) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      {:ok, opts} ->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {:ok,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'         %{policy | check: {check_module, opts}, check_module: check_module, check_opts: opts}}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      {:error, error} ->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {:error, error}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @type context() :: %{resource: Ash.Resource.t()}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @type t :: %__MODULE__{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          check: ref(),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          check_module: module(),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          check_opts: options(),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          type: check_type(),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          __spark_metadata__: Spark.Dsl.Entity.spark_meta()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @doc """\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Strict checks should be cheap, and should never result in external calls (like database or domain)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  It should return `{:ok, true}` if it can tell that the request is authorized, and `{:ok, false}` if\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  update/destroy actions inside a transaction, the existing runtime-check machinery handles\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  the deferral; for create actions, this triggers a post-insert authorization step inside the\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  @callback auto_filter(actor(), authorizer(), options()) ::\n'[39m +
                    [32m'              Keyword.t() | Ash.Expr.t() | :unknown | nil | false\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  @doc """\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  An optional callback, that allows the check to work with policies set to `access_type :runtime`\n'[39m +

                [32m'* actions: read `:read`; create `:create` accepting `user_id`, `org_unit_id`, `role`, `effect`\n'[39m +

                [32m'* `budget_cents` — `:integer`, required, default `0`\n'[39m +

                [32m'`OrgGuard.Access` must define these code-interface functions, so that the verifier can call them and\n'[39m +

                [32m'| `get_org_unit`           | OrgUnit        | `:read`     | fetched by `:id`                                                  |\n'[39m +

                [32m'| `list_role_assignments`  | RoleAssignment | `:read`     |                                                                   |\n'[39m +

                [32m'| `list_documents`         | Document       | `:read`     |                                                                   |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `get_document`           | Document       | `:read`     | fetched by `:id`                                                  |\n'[39m +

                [32m'### Permission resolution (this precedence is normative)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'1. Build the path `U`, `parent(U)`, `parent(parent(U))`, …, up to the root — nearest unit first.\n'[39m +
                [32m'2. For role `R`, walk that path from nearest to root and stop at the **first** unit that carries at\n'[39m +
                [32m'   least one `RoleAssignment` for this actor with that role.\n'[39m +
                [32m'3. If no unit on the path carries such an assignment, the actor does not hold `R` at `U`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'4. If the stopping unit carries **any** assignment for this actor and role with `effect: :deny`,\n'[39m +

                [32m'5. Otherwise the actor holds `R` at `U`.\n'[39m +

                [32m'1. Build the path `U`, `parent(U)`, `parent(parent(U))`, …, up to the root — nearest unit first.\n'[39m +

                [32m'5. Otherwise the actor holds `R` at `U`.\n'[39m +
